correctness.rationale: In normal-angle coordinates the Reuleaux triangle has a three-period curvature square wave with exact odd cubic-frequency coefficients. The support equation h+h''=rho gives coefficients of order \(\ell^{-3}\); Minkowski averaging attenuates frequency \(3\ell\) by \(\cos(3\ell\delta/2)\). The planar Fourier area formula yields the absolutely convergent series (7). Its twice differentiated odd-harmonic cosine sum is exactly evaluated by elementary cosine-series coefficient integration. Boundary conditions at zero and at the reflected-copy disk determine the whole formula. Symbolic checks establish endpoints, derivative, and complementary identity; direct circular-arc support geometry numerically corroborates interior values.

value.rationale: The Reuleaux triangle and disk are the canonical area extremizers among fixed-width planar bodies. A rotated Minkowski mean is a natural exact symmetrization toward the disk, and its relative angle is an intrinsic non-arbitrary parameter on a fundamental 60-degree interval. The all-angle formula supplies the complete area-increase trajectory, strict interior monotonicity, and a surprising complementary-angle conservation identity. It is more informative than the already known endpoint areas and mixed-volume inequalities.
risks: Specific to the classical Reuleaux triangle and equal weights, not a universal area monotonicity principle for arbitrary bodies.
